items.title: Johor education dept offers counselling support after Irene Sofiya's death
items.summary: BATU PAHAT: The Johor Education Department will provide psychological support to the family, teachers and friends of Irene Sofiya Mohd Khairool Faisal, 16, who was murdered at a secondary school in Yong Peng two days ago. Johor Education and Information Committee chairman Dr Muhammad Naqib Md Ghazali said the move was aimed at ensuring their wellbeing and emotional state remained stable. He said the district education office and school principal had met the affected teachers and students for counselling sessions.

items.title: Bolsonaro leads Lula as nail-biter Brazil vote goes to a run-off
items.summary: BRASILIA: Brazilian senator Flavio Bolsonaro, son of the far-right former leader Jair Bolsonaro, finished ahead of President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva in Sunday's election, which will go to a run-off in three weeks. In a surprise result that defied opinion poll projections showing Lula in the lead, Flavio Bolsonaro scored 47 percent of the vote to the incumbent's 45 percent. If Bolsonaro triumphs in the October 25 election, Brazil will be the latest country to swing to the right in Latin America, a trend championed by US President Donald Trump.

items.title: Man electrocuted in suspected cable theft at third-party electrical installation in Klang, says TNB
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Oct 5 — An electrical accident that left a man dead at a 33kV link box along Jalan Abas in Kapar, Klang today occurred at an installation belonging to a third party and not Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB), the utility company said. Sinar Harian reported that TNB said it was alerted to the incident at about 10am and immediately dispatched a technical team to the scene. “TNB will provide its full support and cooperation to the authorities in their investigations,” it said, confirming the incident which was also shared on the TNB Careline Facebook page today.

items.title: Police chase Subaru from Bukit Antarabangsa to Batu Caves, two men arrested over suspected cloned car
items.summary: AMPANG, Oct 5 — Police arrested two local men in their 30s after a chase involving a Subaru that began in Bukit Antarabangsa and ended in Batu Caves, Gombak, early yesterday. Ampang Jaya district police chief Assistant Commissioner Khairul Anuar Khalid said the operation began after the district police headquarters received information about the vehicle at about 4.36am. Khairul Anuar said preliminary checks found that the Subaru was suspected to be a cloned vehicle.

items.title: Nine in 10 workers may feel unprepared for AI as PEOPLElogy launches National AI Readiness Week to get 5 million Malaysians ready by 2030
items.summary: The company has launched National AI Readiness Week 2026 (NAIRW 2026), a five-day national platform to be held from November 12 to 18 across two venues in the Klang Valley. NAIRW 2026 is the flagship national platform of the “I’m AI Ready” movement, a 36-month national drive launched on June 19 this year to get 5 million Malaysians to declare their AI readiness by 2030. Allen Lee, Founder and Managing Director of PEOPLElogy Berhad, says National AI Readiness Week 2026 aims to move Malaysians from AI awareness to real job-ready skills.

items.title: Immigration denies claim 200,000 Thai nationals working at tomyam restaurants
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Immigration Department has denied claims that some 200,000 Thai nationals are working at 5,000 tomyam restaurants in Malaysia. Immigration director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said the Thai cooks comprised 7,559 men and 4,972 women. He said the remaining workers comprised 43 Thai nationals employed as restaurant crew, 38 as eatery workers and seven as restaurant workers.

items.title: FIA chief thanks Malaysia for Sepang F1 comeback
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem has thanked the Malaysian government and public for stepping up to host Formula 1 (F1) in Sepang after a nine-year absence. Ben Sulayem described the operation as an impressive example of motorsport bringing countries together. He said the event demonstrated the value of motorsport in bringing people and countries together.

items.title: Sepang F1 return hinges on five-year business plan: FIA chief Ben Sulayem
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia has been given a clear route back to the Formula 1 (F1) calendar by the world motorsport governing body Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile (FIA). FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem said Sepang International Circuit's return will depend on a credible, long-term business plan backed by the government and strong fan demand. Ben Sulayem said Malaysia has the track, motorsport heritage, and fan base to support a return, but any bid must show that hosting F1 makes commercial, tourism, and economic sense for the country.

items.title: No US vessels in Persian Gulf, Hormuz, or Northern Indian Ocean: IRGC adviser
items.summary: TEHERAN: A senior IRGC adviser says that for the first time, no US vessels are present in the Persian Gulf, the Strait of Hormuz, the Sea of Oman, or even the northern Indian Ocean, The Islamic Republic News Agency (IRNA) reported. Brigadier General Ali Fadavi, head of the advisory group to the commander-in-chief of the Islamic Revolution Guards Corps (IRGC), said in a televised interview that the Strait of Hormuz has been firmly under Iran's control in recent months. The IRGC official said 46 percent of global oil exports passed through the Strait of Hormuz, adding that the 20 percent figure often cited refers to global oil consumption, since many countries consume their own production rather than exporting it.

items.title: Don’t skimp on third-party insurance, and think twice about Waze, Consul General tells Malaysians driving to Thailand
items.summary: SONGKHLA, Oct 5 — Malaysians driving their own vehicles into Thailand are advised to obtain insurance coverage that includes third-party claims in the event of a road accident in the country. Consul General of Malaysia in Songkhla Ahmad Fahmi Ahmad Sarkawi said such insurance is crucial if a Malaysian driver is found to have caused an accident resulting in injury or death, potentially requiring substantial compensation. He also advised Malaysians visiting the country to obtain insurance coverage for vehicle damage caused by natural disasters.

items.title: BN talks with potential Melaka election partners 95pc complete, says Zahid
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Oct 5 — Barisan Nasional (BN) has reached about 95 per cent completion in negotiations with potential partners for the Melaka election, with the coalition expected to reveal the outcome after the election date is announced on Oct 7, its chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said. According to Free Malaysia Today (FMT) Zahid, who is also Umno president, said discussions with the parties involved were nearing completion. Zahid said BN had yet to decide whether PAS would contest the election using the BN logo.

items.title: Four dead, child seriously injured after Axia crashes into lorry on Gerik-Jeli highway
items.summary: Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said police received information about the accident involving three vehicles – a Hino lorry, a Proton Persona and a Perodua Axia – at about 1.30pm yesterday. He said preliminary investigations found that the Perodua Axia, driven by a 19-year-old man with four passengers – a 31-year-old man, a 40-year-old woman and two children – was travelling from Gerik towards Jeli. At the same time, the Proton Persona, driven by a 20-year-old man with three passengers, was travelling in the opposite direction from Jeli, Kelantan towards Gerik, while a lorry driven by a 42-year-old man with a 34-year-old male attendant was also travelling in the same direction.

items.title: Samaiden stays a 'Buy', target price RM3.13
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Samaiden Group Bhd's latest solar project is expected to add about RM200 million to RM250 million in engineering, procurement, construction and commissioning (EPCC) value, according to Hong Leong Investment Bank (HLIB Research). HLIB Research analyst David Ng said the 99.99 megawatt (MWac) award was positive for Samaiden as it lifts the company's cumulative exposure under the Large Scale Solar 5+ (LSS5+) programme to about 200 MWac, or 10.1 per cent of the total awarded capacity. He expects the latest project to contribute to Samaiden's earnings in financial years 2027 and 2028.

items.title: APAC family offices lead on returns as AI, direct deals reshape investing: Citi
items.summary: Citi Wealth's 2026 Global Family Office Report, based on a survey of 351 family offices across 41 countries, found that 26 per cent of APAC respondents achieved year-to-date portfolio returns of more than 15 per cent, the highest among regions surveyed. APAC family offices also set more ambitious return targets, with 22 per cent targeting annual returns above 15 per cent, nearly twice the global average. The report, compiled by Citi Wealth's Global Family Office Group, which works with more than 1,900 family offices worldwide, surveyed clients in June and July, with APAC accounting for 22 per cent of respondents.

items.title: Sultan Ibrahim’s close Bahrain ties helped bring F1 back to Sepang, says Anwar
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 5 — The close ties between His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, and Bahrain’s King Hamad bin Isa Al Khalifa paved the way for Malaysia to host the Formula 1 (F1) Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix (GP), said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. “I pay tribute to His Majesty the King for the leadership and wisdom, and for His Majesty’s close relationship with Bahrain’s King Hamad bin Isa Al Khalifa, which paved the way for Malaysia to be selected as host of the 2026 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix,” he said in a post on X yesterday. The Prime Minister said he joined His Majesty and Bahrain Crown Prince and Prime Minister Prince Salman bin Hamad Al Khalifa to watch the race at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC).

items.title: Father of slain Yong Peng schoolgirl hopes justice will be served, urges public not to speculate
items.summary: BATU PAHAT, Oct 5 — The father of a Form Four student who was found dead at a school in Yong Peng here hopes justice will be served for his daughter. Mohd Khairool Faisal Khyar, 42, said the family was leaving the investigation entirely to police and the relevant authorities to ensure justice for his daughter, Irene Sofiya, 16. Mohd Khairool Faisal also urged the public not to spread inaccurate speculation about the incident involving his daughter, Sinar Harian reported.

items.title: #NSTviral: F1 fans demand Malaysia's permanent return to the F1 calendar
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The roar of Formula One engines at Sepang International Circuit (SIC) has reignited a global clamour for Malaysia's permanent return to the F1 calendar. "We could have the Spanish GP in Malaysia. We could have the Miami GP in Malaysia.

items.title: Anwar praises drivers, teams for ‘incredible action’ at Sepang F1 race
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 5 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim described the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix at the Sepang International Circuit as a deeply meaningful memory for sports fans from around the world. In a Facebook post yesterday, Anwar said the magnificent action delivered by all the drivers and teams also made the race full of excitement and intense competition. Anwar, along with the Crown Prince and Prime Minister of Bahrain, Prince Salman bin Hamad Al Khalifa, also presented trophies to the drivers and teams that triumphed in the race.

items.title: Retiree loses RM367,950 in WhatsApp investment scam
items.summary: Kuala Terengganu police chief Assistant Commissioner Azli Mohd Noor said the victim lodged a police report at 11.49am yesterday. Azli said the suspect subsequently instructed the victim to transfer investment capital in stages to several bank accounts allegedly serving as intermediaries for the scheme. The victim then lodged a police report.

items.title: Ringgit opens higher as weak US jobs data weighs on dollar
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit opened higher against the US dollar on Monday, following reduced expectations of a United States Federal Reserve (Fed) interest rate hike amid weaker-than-expected US jobs data, which is weighing on the greenback. At 8am, the ringgit rose to 4.0805/0870 against the US dollar from Friday's close of 4.0820/0870. Against regional currencies, the ringgit traded mixed.

items.title: Irene Sofiya, 16, laid to rest in Batu Pahat cemetery after school hall death in Yong Peng
items.summary: BATU PAHAT, Oct 5 — Sixteen-year-old Irene Sofiya Mohd Khairool Faisal, who was killed in an incident at a school in Yong Peng, was laid to rest at the Kampung Parit Arshad Muslim Cemetery here at about 7.50pm yesterday. Earlier, her remains were brought to her grandmother’s home in Kampung Parit Selamat, Yong Peng, at about 6.30pm following a post-mortem at Sultanah Nora Ismail Hospital here. The teenager was found unconscious and covered in blood in a school hall in Yong Peng at about 5.50pm yesterday.

items.title: DKU rejects claim Tuanku Muhriz has ceased to be Negeri Sembilan ruler
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Oct 5 — The Negeri Sembilan Dewan Keadilan dan Undang (DKU) has once again reaffirmed that Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir remains the Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan. He said Tuanku Muhriz continued to hold the position, as well as serving as chairman of the DKU under Article 19. Raja Norazli said none of these requirements had been fulfilled.

items.title: Chinese tourist dies after snorkelling off Pom Pom Island
items.summary: In the12.30pm incident, the woman from Yunnan, China, reportedly complained of feeling unwell before asking to be taken back onto the boat. Semporna police chief Superintendent Tan Hiap Wah said the woman was then found unconscious after she was brought onto the boat. He said police were still investigating to determine the circumstances surrounding the incident.

items.title: Reflationist ex-BOJ policymaker calls end to low rates, big spending
items.summary: TOKYO: Japan no longer needs expansionary fiscal and monetary policies aimed at boosting demand, former Bank of Japan (BOJ) board member Asahi Noguchi told Reuters, projecting another interest rate hike by the central bank in December. "Underlying inflation is near the BOJ's 2.0 per cent target and wages are becoming embedded at levels consistent with 2.0 per cent inflation. While the BOJ probably hoped to keep moving cautiously to prevent another economic downturn, it had little choice but to speed up rate hikes to avoid causing unwelcome yen falls, Noguchi said.

items.title: Georgia block party shooting kills two, injures dozens
items.summary: NEW YORK: A shooting early on Sunday at a Georgia block party left two people dead and almost three dozen injured, some critically, local and state officials said. Dooly County Sheriff Craig Peavy told a news conference that two men, aged 21 and 23, were shot dead in Vienna, Georgia, about 135 miles (216 km) south of Atlanta. Thirty-five people were injured, mostly by gunshot wounds, officials told reporters.

items.title: TH investment strategy, risk management among issues in Dewan Rakyat today
items.summary: Datuk Che Mohamad Zulkifly Jusoh (PN-Besut) is scheduled to ask the Prime Minister about measures to diversify TH's investment portfolio and ensure the sustainability of its funds, according to the parliament's order paper. He will also ask about measures being taken to ensure TH can continue helping Malaysians meet the cost of performing the haj. The safety of Malaysians abroad will also come under scrutiny, with Datuk Seri Sh Mohmed Puzi Sh Ali (BN-Pekan) scheduled to ask the foreign minister about measures to strengthen the registration system for Malaysians travelling or staying abroad.

items.title: Oil climbs after Yemeni Houthis attack Saudi Aramco sites
items.summary: SINGAPORE: Oil prices rose on Monday after Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis said they launched ballistic missiles and drones at Saudi Aramco sites in Riyadh and the Khurais area, raising concerns about production at the top exporter in the region. Brent crude futures climbed US$0.81, or 0.79 per cent, to US$103.06 a barrel by 2202 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate crude was at US$91.57 a barrel, up US$0.46, or 0.50 per cent. © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Eight areas hit unhealthy API levels
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Eight areas recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 7am today. Meanwhile, 59 areas recorded moderate API readings, including Batu Muda (99), Bukit Rambai (97), Shah Alam (95), Seremban (93) and Kluang (93). No areas recorded good API readings as of 7am.

items.title: Iran's oil minister resigns, president appoints replacement
items.summary: ISTANBUL: Iranian Oil Minister Mohsen Paknejad has resigned, Iran's state-run Tasnim news agency reported Sunday, citing a presidential official, according to Anadolu Ajansi. Mehdi Tabatabaei, deputy head of communications at the Iranian president's office, said President Masoud Pezeshkian has accepted Paknejad's resignation. No reason was given for Paknejad's resignation, which came amid unprecedented US sanctions on Iran, particularly targeting its oil sector.

items.title: Lee should have served out term despite PKR differences, says Hassan
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Lee Chean Chung should have continued serving as Petaling Jaya member of parliament until the end of his term regardless of his differences with PKR or its president Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, says one of the party's senior MPs. Pasir Gudang MP Hassan Abdul Karim said Lee should have followed the example of Sembrong MP Datuk Seri Hishammuddin Hussein, who continued serving his constituency and attending Parliament despite being suspended from Umno. "It is not proper for Lee to resign as Petaling Jaya MP.

items.title: Bank Islam's pivot to profitability over volume in the digital era
items.summary: Therefore, the appointment of former chief executive officer (CEO) of Aeon Bank, Datin Paduka Raja Teh Maimunah Raja Abdul Aziz, as well as former CEO of Ryt Bank, Melvin Ooi, to lead Bank Islam Malaysia Bhd attracts the attention of those within the industry. How would Raja Teh, who also hailed from Ambank Group prior to her stint at Aeon Bank – she was the CEO of AmInvestment Bank and managing director of the group's wholesale banking – drive Bank Islam forward in an era of digitalisation, alongside Ooi? For Raja Teh, chasing loan growth for the sake of expansion will no longer be the game for Bank Islam.

items.title: Transforming Bank Islam's digital architecture, embracing open finance to better serve customers
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The appointment of Melvin Ooi, the former chief executive officer (CEO) of Ryt Bank – one of the earlier digital banks in Malaysia – as the chief technology and transformation officer (CTTO) of Bank Islam shows the bank's aggressive push towards digitalisation. Ooi noted that transforming a 43-year-old legacy bank's digital architecture poses a unique challenge compared to starting a digital bank from scratch. "After building a digital bank, the opportunity of transforming a legacy bank is too hard to resist," said Ooi.

items.title: Can Malaysia break the FBM KLCI's 'lost decade' curse?
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's stock market is approaching a critical test as two major reforms take shape, but whether they can finally help it break out of what many describe as its "lost decade" remains an open question. The FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) continues to trade below its historical valuation despite the country's economic expansion over the past decade, which has fuelled business growth and earnings. The firm's research head Imran Yassin Md Yusof said the experiences of stock markets in Singapore, Japan and South Korea show that prolonged stagnation need not be permanent, and Malaysia could follow a similar path.

items.title: Norway turned oil into wealth
items.summary: Norway and the United Kingdom discovered major petroleum resources in broadly the same North Sea geological system at roughly the same historical moment. But it accumulated no comparable national petroleum fund. Britain largely converted North Sea petroleum into public revenue.

items.title: Sustainability, AI, and the new era of corporate reporting
items.summary: Traditionally, the path to becoming a professional accountant has centred on mastering technical accounting-related competencies such as financial reporting, auditing, taxation, and management accounting. With sustainability reporting, and artificial intelligence (AI) gaining global momentum, our graduates are rightfully wondering what this means for their careers. In Malaysia, sustainability reporting is also moving from largely voluntary practice toward formal regulatory requirements.

items.title: Simpan SSPN turns savings into big dreams
items.summary: BUKIT MERTAJAM: Beneath BMS 2026's colourful "Under the Sea" theme lies a simple message: start saving today so children can sail towards tomorrow. Simpan SSPN Plus 2026 Draw — Cabutan WOW! Simpan SSPN Plus 2026, Series 2 category.

items.title: Pro-Imran Khan march starts in Pakistan's northwest
items.summary: LAKKI MARWAT, Pakistan: A march protesting the imprisonment of former Pakistani prime minister Imran Khan kicked off Sunday in the country's northwest after talks to avoid the demonstration stalled. Authorities have been preparing for weeks for the possible arrival of demonstrators in Islamabad, with the march planned by supporters of Khan's Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party originally slated for September 27 and then postponed until Sunday. Sohail Afridi, the chief minister for Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, said earlier on X that the demonstration in support of Khan would go ahead.

items.title: Amanah, DAP differ over PH cooperation with Bersatu in Melaka
items.summary: MELAKA: Parti Amanah Negara is at odds with DAP over possible political cooperation between Pakatan Harapan and other political coalitions or parties for the Melaka election. He said sincerity among coalition partners was important as it formed the basis for a stable government. "Amanah's position is to seek sincere partners to govern Melaka.

items.title: Suhakam doesn’t need prosecutorial powers — but govt must answer its findings, says chairman
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 5 — The Human Rights Commission of Malaysia (Suhakam) does not need prosecutorial powers to be effective, but authorities should be required to respond to its findings and recommendations, its chairman Datuk Seri Mohd Hishamudin Md Yunus said. “Suhakam’s present mandate is primarily investigative, advisory, educational and recommendatory. “Suhakam already has important investigative powers under Act 597 (the Suhakam Act).

items.title: J-KOM boosting communication efforts on social media
items.summary: SEBERANG PRAI: The Community Communications Department (J-KOM) is placing greater emphasis on social media, giving it 70 per cent of its communication efforts to ensure government messages and achievements reach the people. "Without a strong presence on social media, government messages will not reach the grassroots. "PMK complements this by explaining government policies and achievements directly to the people, especially when negative messages circulating on social media can overshadow these achievements," he said after a PMK event here yesterday.

items.title: Malaysia, Thailand boost flood aid coordination
items.summary: Malaysia's Consul-General in Songkhla Ahmad Fahmi Ahmad Sarkawi said this was part of preparations to deal with the possibility of major floods such as those that hit Hat Yai last November. He said warehouses that could be used to store supplies from Malaysia had been identified. He said if Thai authorities did not have enough manpower, non-governmental organisations from Malaysia could help.

items.title: Middle East carriers fight back
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia and other Asia-Pacific aviation markets could face stronger competition for international passengers as Middle Eastern airlines seek to win back traffic lost to Asian carriers following disruptions earlier this year. Association of Asia Pacific Airlines (AAPA) director-general Wong Hong told Business Times: "You may get some shift, but Middle Eastern carriers are not going to give up without a fight. Since tensions began in the Middle East, several Asia-Pacific airlines have seen an increase in transit traffic as passengers opted for alternative routes through Asian hubs.

items.title: Sabah gives more than 500 adults second chance to learn reading, writing, counting
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Oct 4 — More than 500 adults in Sabah who missed out on formal education are being given a second chance to master basic reading, writing and counting (3M) skills through the Functional Literacy Education Programme (PLF) organised by the Community Development Department (KEMAS). Sabah KEMAS director Ahmad Fakhrul Azman Muhammad Radzi said the participants are attending 25 classes this year in urban fringe, rural and remote areas across Kudat, Kota Marudu, Kota Belud, Keningau, Tenom, Nabawan, Beluran, Sandakan, Kinabatangan, Lahad Datu, Semporna, Tawau and Kalabakan. Before joining the classes, participants sit for a pre-test to assess their initial reading, writing and counting skills.

items.title: Anwar: F1 excitement at Sepang also brings opportunities for local traders
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 4 — The return of Formula 1 (F1) to the Sepang International Circuit (SIC) after a nine-year absence has not only delighted motorsport fans but also provided an opportunity for about 40 local traders to earn an income through the Karnival Litar Rasa Madani. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the carnival, held at the G Hillstand at SIC in conjunction with the 2026 F1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix (GP), brought together local traders offering a variety of food and beverages, including snacks and light refreshments. He said that the lively atmosphere at the circuit also gave visitors an opportunity to enjoy local fare while watching the race and, at the same time, supporting local traders.

items.title: Zahid urges UiTM to establish Quantum Department, says Malaysia must not lag
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Oct 4 — Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has called on Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM) to establish a Quantum Department to ensure the country does not lag behind current advancements. Ahmad Zahid, who is also the Rural and Regional Development Minister, said this after officiating the ‘Wacana Semarak Patriotisme: Seminar Ilmuwan Islam’ at the university’s Dewan Agung Tuanku Canselor here today. Ahmad Zahid said his ministry would also contribute RM500,000 to UiTM to support the development of programmes such as the TVET UiTM Dihatiku training and certification programme and UTAMA PLUS UiTM AI Certified, including the development of the Quantum Department.

items.title: Malaysia eyes F1 calendar return as PM Anwar confirms talks under way
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 4 — Malaysia is discussing a possible return to the Formula One calendar beyond this weekend’s race at Sepang, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said today, raising hopes of a longer-term revival of the Malaysian Grand Prix. Anwar confirmed the talks during a brief exchange with Sky Sports commentator Martin Brundle on the grid at the Sepang International Circuit ahead of today’s Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia. The remark is the clearest indication yet that Putrajaya is considering extending Malaysia’s renewed association with Formula One beyond this weekend, which marked the sport’s first race at Sepang in nine years.

items.title: Brunei Sultan departs after witnessing F1 Gulf Air Bahrain GP return to Sepang
items.summary: SEPANG, Oct 4 — The Sultan of Brunei, Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah, departed for home today after concluding his special visit in conjunction with the Formula 1 (F1) Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix (GP) at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC). Earlier, Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah attended the F1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix at SIC with His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, and the top leaders of Malaysia, Bahrain and Brunei to witness the return of the prestigious F1 race to Sepang after a nine-year absence. Also attending the race were Bahrain Crown Prince and Prime Minister Prince Salman bin Hamad Al Khalifa and Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.

items.title: Boy mauled by pack of five stray dogs in Bachok receives rabies jab, shows signs of recovery
items.summary: The boy’s mother, Rosnani Mat Salleh, 46, said her son, Azuar Firdaus Zuraiman, showed positive progress today after remaining withdrawn for two days as he was still traumatised by the incident. Recalling the incident, Rosnani said Azuar Firdaus was playing on the beach around 9.30 am with three relatives when five stray dogs approached. Rosnani said her son underwent a five-hour surgery the day after the incident to treat his injuries.

items.title: Amanah says Pakatan open to partners to form stable Melaka govt ahead of state election
items.summary: MELAKA, Oct 4 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) is open to seeking allies to form a stable government in Melaka in the upcoming state election, said Amanah secretary-general Muhammad Faiz Fadzil. He said Amanah’s stand was that it was better for the coalition to find partners who could work together to form a stable state government. Muhammad Faiz said any decision on political cooperation would be determined by the PH Presidential Council, but Amanah had been exploring collaboration with various parties.

items.title: Another woman files report against motivational speaker as Perlis police probe alleged sexual harassment
items.summary: KANGAR, Oct 4 — Perlis police have confirmed receiving another report against a male motivational speaker over an allegation of sexual harassment. Perlis police chief DCP Hamzah Hashim said the report was received yesterday and involved a 19-year-old female complainant. He said the motivational speaker would be released on police bail before being re-arrested by Kangar police for further action.

items.title: Motorcycle skids towards drain near Taiping, killing 76-year-old rider
items.summary: IPOH, Oct 4 — An elderly man was killed and a woman who was the pillion rider was seriously injured after the motorcycle they were riding skidded at Lorong Kampung Boyan 1, Kampung Boyan near Taiping, today. Perak Fire and Rescue Department Assistant Director of Operations Sabarodzi Nor Ahmad said the 76-year-old man was pronounced dead at the scene by Ministry of Health (MOH) medical officers. Sabarodzi said firefighters lifted the male victim, who was nearly falling into the drain, before MOH medical officers confirmed his death.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan joins Johor on unhealthy air list as haze lingers
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 4 — A total of eight locations recorded Air Pollutant Index (API) readings in the unhealthy category as of 4pm today. According to the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, five areas in Johor were affected, involving Segamat (156), Batu Pahat (155), Kluang (152), Tangkak (151) and Larkin (111). Meanwhile, 57 areas were in the moderate category, while three areas recorded good readings.

items.title: F1 roars back at Sepang as Sultan Ibrahim, Bahrain and Brunei royals watch on
items.summary: SEPANG, Oct 4 — The return of Formula 1 to the Sepang International Circuit (SIC) after a nine-year absence received special attention today when His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, attended the 2026 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix F1 race, together with the top leaders of Malaysia, Bahrain and Brunei. His Majesty was received on arrival at about 2.15 pm by Bahrain Crown Prince and Prime Minister Prince Salman bin Hamad Al Khalifa and Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. Also attending the race were the Sultan of Brunei, Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah, and Prince Abdul Mateen Bolkiah, who were received by Anwar at about 2.35 pm.

items.title: After F1 and KL Marathon, October’s only getting busier with Melaka election dates on Wednesday and Budget Friday
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 4 — October has got off to a positive start for Malaysia, marked by a vibrant sporting calendar, strong performances by national athletes and encouraging developments in the economy and investment, while several major national agendas await as the month unfolds. The first weekend of the month saw Malaysia become a focal point for sports fans as the roar of Formula 1 (F1) machinery once again echoed at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC) after nine years, with Malaysia hosting the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia 2026. Malaysia’s investment momentum also received a boost as the country and Singapore explored efforts to attract third-country investors to the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ).

items.title: Petros assurance rings hollow amid challenge to Petronas, says Zaid
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 4 — Former law minister Datuk Zaid Ibrahim says Sarawak premier Abang Johari Openg’s assurance that Petros will not undermine Petronas rings hollow while the state oil company seeks a bigger role in the gas business and Sarawak continues to question the federal legal framework governing petroleum. Writing on Facebook, Zaid said the central issue was Petros’s desire to take over the gas aggregator role currently performed by Petronas in Sarawak. He estimated Petronas’s Sarawak gas business at about RM10 billion annually.

items.title: JPJ hunts illegal motorcycle ride operators ferrying passengers to Sepang F1 circuit
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 4 — The Road Transport Department (JPJ) is tracking down individuals and groups offering illegal motorcycle ride-hailing services to transport visitors and spectators attending the Formula One (F1) Bahrain Grand Prix at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC). According to Berita Harian , the operators were found advertising their services through various social media platforms, offering rides from several locations to the circuit grounds and between SIC and nearby parking areas. A survey of social media postings showed that both car and motorcycle transport services were being promoted, although motorcycles appeared to be the preferred option among spectators seeking to avoid heavy traffic congestion around the circuit.

items.title: Government to follow legal process over Bandar Utama school stabbing suit, says deputy law minister
items.summary: IPOH, Oct 4 — The government will allow due process to take its course following a civil suit filed by the family of a 16-year-old girl who was killed in a stabbing incident at a school in Bandar Utama last year, Deputy Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) M. Kulasegaran said today. Asked whether existing laws should be strengthened to include mental health provisions, Kulasegaran said the government was not currently drafting any new legislation on the matter. He also stressed the importance of helping parents better understand their children’s needs, including mental health concerns.

items.title: Water in the tank at Batu Kawan? Penang team looks into viral claims of vehicle trouble after refuelling
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Oct 4 — The Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry (KPDN) in Penang is investigating claims that several vehicles experienced problems after refuelling at petrol stations near Batu Kawan. “The Penang KPDN has taken note of the claims of vehicles experiencing problems after refuelling at a petrol station near Batu Kawan. Earlier, several posts went viral on social media alleging that vehicles experienced problems, including being unable to start, after refuelling at several petrol stations around Penang.

items.title: Rapid KL adds eight more shuttle buses as MRT Putrajaya Line repair work continues
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 4 — Repair works are underway to restore power supply and train services on the Putrajaya Line following a cable theft near the Taman Equine MRT Station, according to Rapid KL. It said alternative train services and free shuttle buses remained available to help passengers get to their destinations during the disruption. “Alternative train services and free shuttle buses are still operating to assist passengers, with eight additional buses deployed to facilitate passenger movement,” it said in a statement.

items.title: Raincoat and umbrella check: Storm warning for KL, Putrajaya and six states until 4pm
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 4 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning for thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds in Kuala Lumpur, Putrajaya and six states until 4 pm today. A similar warning was also issued for Kelantan (Pasir Puteh and Bachok) as well as Terengganu (Besut, Setiu, Kuala Nerus and Kuala Terengganu). In Sarawak, the affected areas are Limbang (Limbang), Miri (Marudi), Sri Aman (Sri Aman and Lubok Antu), Betong (Betong), Bintulu (Tatau), Sibu (Selangau) and Kapit (Song).
